To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new model for the short rate, that is based on a telegraphic process, that we have derived closed form solutions for the zero coupon bonds and that these closed form solutions are in very good agreement with the solutions that are based on numerical solutions of the partial differential equation.
the convexity adjustment is a function of the jump size, the intensity of the jumps and the time to maturity.

we have obtained a closed formula for the zero coupon price in a Markov-modulation jump-diffusion model for the short rate and we have obtained a system of PDEs for the price of the zero coupon bond using no-arbitrage assumptions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) How to price a bond using a Markov-modulate jump-diffusion process for the short rate?
the pricing and convexity adjustment of zero coupon bonds under a Markov-modulation jump-diffusion model.
the pricing of zero coupon bonds in Markov-modulated jumpdiffusion models for the interest rate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the convexity adjustment is not negligible and that the jump-diffusion model is more accurate than the diffusion one.
the convexity adjustment is negligible for the short maturity bonds, but it increases with the maturity.
the convexity-adjusted price is a better approximation to the true bond price than the unadjusted price.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our model is able to explain the convexity effect in the zero coupon bond market and the magnitude of the adjustment is consistent with market prices.
we provide closed formulas for the short rate and the zero coupon bond prices.
the jump component in the short rate is not a significant source of convexity adjustment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the convexity-adjusted price of a zero-coupon bond can be computed by using the Markov-modulated short rate model.
the convexity adjustment can be significant in the short term and that it is not negligible in the medium and long term.
the jump-diffusion model is a better fit than the diffusion model to describe short rates and zero coupon bond prices, especially in the presence of jumps.
